title: Utility-weighted physical expert copies vs logical Views
hypothesis: Allocating full physical copies to high-utility children and compact Views to aligned low-utility children improves the quality/bytes/compute frontier over all-copy, all-View and random-copy policies.
physical_object: one parent expert with a shared residual basis and optional selected full child copies
mirror_coordinate: per-child scalar basis coefficient for logical copies
logical_multiplicity: sixteen child expert functions with utility-weighted physical allocation
controls: random hybrid at equal physical count

development.selection_metric: utility-weighted heldout output error, total payload bytes, physical copies and code inference MAC

fresh.reason: native low-rank control exactly aliases View; keep as one development screen

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: A utility-ranked hybrid must beat all-copy and all-View quality/byte/compute Pareto at equal utility-weighted error and outperform random copy selection at equal K.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror specificity if native low-rank matches View behavior, actual bytes erase hybrid savings, or utility selection does not beat random at equal K.
boundaries: Synthetic linear child functions and frequency weights only; no trained MoE utility estimator or pretraining cost claim.
The top two utility children include private residual variation by construction.
No claim that observed fixed-budget gains increase model capacity.
